product: Mitapivat (PYRUKYND, AQVESME), an oral pyruvate kinase activator approved for PK deficiency (2022) and thalassemia (US 2026, EU May 2026), with a sickle cell sNDA under FDA priority review. Pipeline: AG-236 siRNA in polycythemia vera, AG-181 in PKU, cevidoplenib in ITP; tebapivat discontinued.
demand: Demand comes from a new thalassemia indication launch plus geographic expansion, not price: mitapivat net revenue rose to 44.7M USD in Q2 2026 from 12.5M USD a year earlier, with 442 cumulative AQVESME prescriptions as of Jun 30 2026.
pricing_power: Moderate: mitapivat is first-in-class oral PK activator and the only medicine EU-approved for the broad adult thalassemia population, with orphan designations; no price increases were cited, so reported growth reflects volume and indication mix.
competition: Sickle cell: gene therapies (Vertex/CRISPR Casgevy, bluebird Lyfgenia), hydroxyurea and Novartis; thalassemia: luspatercept (BMS) and gene therapy; ITP: first-generation SYK inhibitors and TPO receptor agonists; PK deficiency: no approved competitor.
team: CEO Brian Goff and Chief Medical Officer and Head of R&D Sarah Gheuens, M.D., Ph.D. lead the company; both are quoted in the 2026 releases on commercial launch and pipeline execution.
market_strategy: Execute the AQVESME thalassemia launch, win the mitapivat sickle cell indication, diversify rare hematology through in-licensed late-stage assets such as cevidoplenib, and keep capital discipline with 964.8M USD cash for operational independence.
bull: Mitapivat revenue grew to 44.7M USD in Q2 2026 from 12.5M, driven by AQVESME thalassemia launch; FDA priority review of sickle cell sNDA with Nov 1 2026 PDUFA; 5 of 6 recent analyst actions were raises.
bear: RISE UP Phase 3 missed the pain-crisis co-primary and fatigue secondary; tebapivat failed in sickle cell Jul 21 2026; Q2 net loss 100.7M on 44.7M revenue; cash fell 1.2B to 964.8M in six months; RBC and Goldman Hold at 32 USD.
falsifier: FDA issues a CRL or delays the mitapivat sickle cell sNDA past the Nov 1 2026 PDUFA date.
web_what_changed: Last 90 days: Jun 1 licensed cevidoplenib from Oscotec, 25M USD upfront; Jun 13 EHA RISE UP Phase 3 sickle cell data; Jul 7 FDA priority review of mitapivat sNDA in sickle cell, PDUFA Nov 1 2026; Jul 21 tebapivat Phase 2 discontinued in sickle cell; Jul 30 Q2 results, mitapivat net revenue 44.7M USD vs 12.5M.
web_not_known_yesterday: not found (no new Agios primary disclosure since Jul 30 2026; only a Sep 21 2026 BofA target raise to 50 USD, aggregator).
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Growth is volume and mix, not price: Q2 2026 mitapivat net revenue 44.7M USD (40.9M US, 3.8M ex-US) driven by the AQVESME thalassemia launch in the US from late Jan 2026, EU approval in May 2026 and Gulf demand; 442 cumulative AQVESME prescriptions as of Jun 30 2026.
web_suppliers: not found (no named suppliers disclosed). Agios depends on third-party contract manufacturers for drug substance and product; Avanzanite Bioscience distributes in Europe; Oscotec is licensor, not a supplier.
web_customers: not found (concentration not disclosed). End customers are patients and prescribers; US distribution runs through REMS-certified physicians and specialty pharmacies, ex-US through Avanzanite Bioscience in the EU and GCC distributors.
web_who_loses: Sickle cell gene therapies (Vertex/CRISPR Casgevy, bluebird bio Lyfgenia), Novartis crizanlizumab, Pfizer voxelotor (withdrawn) and Agios own tebapivat (discontinued); in thalassemia luspatercept (BMS) and gene therapy; in ITP first-generation SYK inhibitor fostamatinib.
web_contradicting_evidence: RISE UP Phase 3 met hemoglobin response (40.6% vs 2.9%) but MISSED the co-primary pain-crisis endpoint and the fatigue key secondary; tebapivat failed in sickle cell (Jul 21 2026) and LR-MDS (May 29 2026); Q2 net loss 100.7M USD on 44.7M revenue; cash fell 1.2B to 964.8M in six months; RBC and Goldman sit at Hold with 32 USD targets.
web_if_management_right: FDA approves mitapivat for sickle cell disease by Nov 1 2026, making it the first oral PK activator there; AQVESME thalassemia launch scales; AG-236, AG-181 and cevidoplenib advance, lifting revenue from a small base toward stated 1B USD peak US sales potential.
web_if_management_wrong: A CRL or delay on the sickle cell sNDA, or REIGNITE failure that withdraws accelerated approval, stalls revenue near 45M USD a quarter against roughly 150M USD quarterly opex, forcing dilution and validating the 32 USD bear targets.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Oscotec (milestones and tiered royalties), Avanzanite Bioscience (EU commercial partner), contract manufacturers and specialty distributors, and the wider PK-activation class validated across hemolytic anemias; reduced transfusion burden benefits sickle cell supportive-care providers.
